## 1. The owned slave and the one given provision  (`#the-slave-and-the-one-given-provision`)

Cited ayat: 16:75-76

> **16:75** ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا عَبْدًا مَّمْلُوكًا لَّا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ وَمَن رَّزَقْنَٰهُ مِنَّا رِزْقًا حَسَنًا فَهُوَ يُنفِقُ مِنْهُ سِرًّا وَجَهْرًا هَلْ يَسْتَوُۥنَ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
>
> **16:76** وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَّجُلَيْنِ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَبْكَمُ لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ وَهُوَ كَلٌّ عَلَىٰ مَوْلَىٰهُ أَيْنَمَا يُوَجِّههُّ لَا يَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِى هُوَ وَمَن يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ

### Claims

**c1** (16:75): God struck a similitude: a slave who is owned and has power over nothing, and one to whom God gave good provision from Himself, so that he spends from it in secret and openly; the ayah asks whether they are equal.

**c2** (16:75): The ayah says that all praise is for God, but that most of them do not know.

**c3** (16:76): God also struck a similitude of a pair of men, one of whom is dumb, has power over nothing and is a burden on his master, and brings no good wherever he sends him.

**c4** (16:76): The ayah asks whether he is equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path.

### One-minute summary

God struck a similitude of a slave who is owned and has power over nothing, and of one given good provision who spends from it in secret and openly, and asks whether they are equal [c1]. He also struck a similitude of a man who is dumb and a burden on his master, and asks whether he is equal to one who commands justice [c3][c4].

### Complete story

God struck a similitude: a slave who is owned and has power over nothing, and one to whom God gave good provision from Himself, so that he spends from it in secret and openly [c1]. The ayah asks whether they are equal [c1]. It says that all praise is for God, but that most of them do not know [c2].

God also struck a similitude of a pair of men [c3]. One of them is dumb, has power over nothing and is a burden on his master, and brings no good wherever he sends him [c3]. The ayah asks whether he is equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path [c4].

### Deep study

Each similitude is built as a contrast followed by a question: are they equal [c1][c4]. The first contrast is between having power over nothing and spending from good provision given by God [c1]. The next is between one who brings no good and one who commands justice and is on a straight path [c3][c4].

### Kids mode

God struck a similitude of a slave who is owned and has power over nothing, and of one given good provision who spends from it in secret and openly [c1]. The ayah asks whether they are equal [c1]. It says that all praise is for God [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the first similitude sets having power over nothing beside spending from provision that God gave [c1]. Another reading is that the later similitude sets one who brings no good beside one who commands justice and is on a straight path [c3][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the men in these similitudes are; the ayat name no one and do not say whether the pictures are about particular persons.
- Not established: what the similitudes are about in the passage around them; the question are they equal is all the ayat state.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later sources link the pair of men to particular people; this draft does not repeat or vouch for them.
- The ayat themselves use the word for a similitude (mathal) in both places.
